Messages.Author: Matthieu Miyamoto
Messages.Body:
On Thu, 23 Jan 1997, David wrote:

> I'm not sure if this is the right card: I mean the one that costs 2 blood,
> put five blood on, taken as D action by sabbat vampires. Can you (the person
> who played the card) take the blood off the powerbase as D action? Who is the
> action directed against?
>

Nope, wrong card. Your talking about, Powerbase: Mexico City. But it is
exactly the card that you are talking about.
Unfortunatly, you cannot take (D) actions against yourself.
Instruction book, Advanced Blocking 18.1, page 39.
"Directed Actions directly affect another Methuselah or one of his
minions."
The D action is directed at you.

This card sucks. I wouldnt call it broken though. I don't believe that
any card should be considered broken, because of the fact that it has
been made, and players should deal with it and play with it if they want
to or not. Some cards are there because it fit the criteria of fun, in
case anyone has forgotten that. Anyone who has played a "fun"
malkavian deck(no, not stealth bleed, or hidden weopon, stereo typical
deck). But just have fun, (although it might be a new concept to some
people... hahaha =p ). Start playing Monacle of Clarity,
or Madness of the bard. Or start playing blood games, with malkavian
pranks and malkavian game. It shouldnt matter if you lose playing that
game, because it is fun.
This card is part of a good strategy. You put this card out, to let
other people attempt to steal the blood off it as a variant to combat
rush. Let them try to steal it then catch them, and send them to torpor.

M.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Rob LeGood <rfle...@ix.netcom.com> writes:
>David wrote:
>> I'm not sure if this is the right card: I mean the one that costs 2 blood,
>> put five blood on, taken as D action by sabbat vampires. Can you (the person
>> who played the card) take the blood off the powerbase as D action? Who is the
>> action directed against?

> From what our group has come to understand...
>1) Yes, you're own vampire can remove all the blood. (This one I'm
>positive about)

This is incorrect. You can never, under any circumstances, direct
a (D) action at yourself or anything you control.
Explicit or implicit card text is needed to overcome this restriction
(Rampage has implicit card text).

>2) The directed action is against yourself, and hence unblockable. (Not
>as positive, but I believe there are ruling which support this.

This would be true, if you could direct the (D) action against
yourself (and is true in the case of Rampage).

First, I'll respond to the initial post, then to the response by Rob.

: David wrote:

: > Can you (the person who played the card) take the blood off the
: > powerbase as D action? Who is the action directed against?

Yes, it's the right card. No, one of your own vampires may NOT take
the blood. This is by rule of directed actions AND card text... I believe
that it states that a vampire of ANOTHER Meth. can take the blood as a (D)
action. The text (as pulled from the Rulemonger's site) is below. Please
correct if necessary.

Powerbase: New York Master 1 pool
UNIQUE LOCATION. As a master phase action, you may burn 1 pool to
move 3 blood counters from the blood bank to this card or move one
blood counter from this card to your pool. Any Sabbat vampire
controlled by another Methuselah can take a (D) action to move all
the blood on the 'base to his or her controller's blood pool. Burn
this card when the last blood counter on it is removed.
Artist: Ted Naifeh Rarity: Uncommon

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Justin Grace wrote:
>
> In article <5c851s$1...@redwood.cs.sc.edu>, "L. Scott Johnson"
> <sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu> writes
> >This is incorrect. You can never, under any circumstances, direct
> >a (D) action at yourself or anything you control.
> >Explicit or implicit card text is needed to overcome this restriction
> >(Rampage has implicit card text).
>
> What card text does Darius Styx have?

As a (D) action, Darius may pick one card at random from a
Methuselah's hand...

(Note that it says "a", not "any" - this card text is available
from WotC's web page.) Not that it would make any difference
either way, officially, but the distinction should help clear up
the supposed "implied" self-directability.

> I know it's been ruled for the old
> tournament rules that he couldn't pull cards from his controller's hand,
> but these tournament rules don't affect how we play.

The ruling is not a "for tournament play" rule any more than the ruling
that you can bleed any Methuselah with Computer Hacking (by virtue of
the (D) symbol) is only "for tournament play".

These are the official rulings. For all play.

The only "for tournament play" rulings are:

* No repeat actions
* PAs burned for votes are not replaced until the end of the current turn.
* Libraries may not include cards from the banned list
* <Some time limit stuff>

> Also, the card text is very iffy and seems to imply that you can direct
> the action at yourself ('any Methuselah' *does* include the controller,
> since he/she *is* a Methuselah...)

Note the similarity of form with Ambush:

(D) Enter combat with a tapped minion.

Now, are you saying that Ambush implies that you can attack your own
minions? If so, allow me to clear up that point as well: You can't.

Also, Arson:

(D) Burn a location. (Jyhad adds: "Can be directed at any Methuselah.")

Neither of these actually overrides the restriction against directing a
(D) action at yourself, so they cannot be used to burn a location that
you control.

--
L. Scott Johnson (vte...@regency.wizards.com)

At no time, past or present, have the DCI's tournament rules for VTES
ever made statments about Darius Styx's special ability. Up until this
most recent release of tournament rules, the DCI never made any
statements that altered in any way the _rules_ of the game. They have
never made any specific card rulings.
